title: Tiered token-bucket admission with SLA-weighted response slimming and multi-region circuit breaker
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During region-level capacity pressure and bursty tenant traffic we observe tail-latency SLO violations and noisy neighbor effects. Existing shedding approaches (single global queues or purely probabilistic shedding) either cause unpredictable client latency or disproportionate quality loss for high-SLA tenants.

Goal: Implement a deterministic, hierarchical admission controller that enforces configured token-bucket rates per SLA tier and per-tenant, integrates with region-aware circuit breakers for graceful multi-region failover, and applies lightweight response slimming when requests are admitted but the system is degraded. The solution should be observable, testable under chaos scenarios, and support incremental rollout.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Tiered Token Buckets: Maintain a small hierarchy of token buckets: global pool, region pool, SLA-tier buckets (gold/silver/bronze), and per-tenant leaky bucket. Admission consumes tokens from the SLA bucket first, falling back to region/global when configured spill-over is enabled. Buckets are coordinated at control-plane level using lightweight leases and eventual reconciliation to avoid cross-region races.
2) SLA-weighted response slimming: When tokens are scarce but a request is admitted due to high SLA weight, apply response slimming rules instead of outright rejection. Response slimming is a deterministic sequence of non-destructive degradations (e.g., truncate max tokens, disable auxiliary reranking step, switch to quantized model variant, drop peripheral metadata). Each SLA tier has ordered slimming profiles and a max cumulative quality delta budget.
3) Region-aware circuit breakers: Track region health signals (p95 latency, error rate, infra-saturated flag) and trip a regional breaker into three modes: OPEN (reject new admissions except emergency tenants), THROTTLE (enforce aggressive bucket ratios + slimming), and DEGRADED (prioritize cross-region failover routing). Breaker state transitions are recorded and surfaced to the Console with suggested rollout actions.
4) Migration & rollout: Start with simulation and shadowing for a subset of tenants, then staged canary in a single region, followed by multi-region canary with controlled spill-over. Add feature flags to dynamically toggle slimming levels.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Determinism chosen over pure probabilistic shedding to give product teams predictable behavior and easier debugging.
- Slimming actions must be reversible and have clear telemetry hooks to measure quality impact (per-prompt evals and downstream user metrics).
- Token synchronization across regions should favor availability: rely on local enforcement with periodic reconciliation instead of strict global coordination.
- Integrate with existing rollout and fallback infra: routing policies, model variants registry, and Console dashboards.

Success metrics:
- Reduce number of p99 latency SLO breaches during region incidents by 60% compared to baseline incident runbooks.
- Maintain >=95% request acceptance for Gold tenants under 2x baseline load while keeping p95 latency within SLO.
- Measurement pipeline emits per-tenant quality delta when slimming applied, and total cost delta per token saved.
acceptance_criteria: Hierarchical token-bucket admission implemented in runtime control plane with config for global/region/SLA/tenant buckets
SLA-weighted slimming pipeline implemented with at least three reversible slimming steps and per-tenant profile support
Region circuit breaker with OPEN/THROTTLE/DEGRADED states wired to admission decisions and routing suggestions
End-to-end integration tests including chaos scenario for region failover and automated canary gating
Dashboard panels in Console showing bucket utilization, breaker state, slimming events and per-tenant quality delta
Documentation: design doc, runbook for on-call, and rollout playbook with rollback criteria

comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created after postmortem for 2026-02-28 region incident. Noting noisy neighbor impact on Gold tenants despite reserved capacity due to request amplification. Started draft design.

2026-03-11 - Ravi Patel: Spike complete: local prototype uses per-worker token buckets with lightweight gossip; measured <2% admission variance across workers under synthetic burst. Attaching benchmark gist. Deciding to prefer eventual consistency to keep fast local enforcement.

2026-03-11 - Mei Chen (PM): Please ensure slimmed responses emit 'quality_level' header so product teams can detect UX regressions. Also request a fallthrough policy for customers to opt into 'best-effort' semantics.

2026-03-12 - Security review (junior): Reviewed slimmed payload surface — flagged that disabling reranking may remove PII derived features. Marked for design note to ensure no user PII is dropped unexpectedly.
